reviews.one_line_contribution: A measurement study that asks how many fewer leave-one-out re-runs are needed to rank memory items reliably when the same re-runs are scored by process endpoints (goal-condition progress, steps-to-success, first-divergence step) instead of the binary success flag, and which manufactured item classes those endpoints systematically mis-value.
reviews.closest_prior_work: VERIFIED: EarlyEval, arXiv:2609.02783 (2026-09-02, confirmed via the literature command on both channels; abstract: trains LightGBM success/failure classifiers over behavioral, textual and reference-solution features and halts an agent run when either crosses a calibrated threshold). This is one week older than the proposal and is structurally the same object as E7: a calibrated classifier of success fitted on process features to buy the same evaluation at lower cost. It does not threaten the per-item counterfactual framing (EarlyEval cuts cost within a task for aggregate accuracy; it never estimates the value of a removed item, never runs a leave-one-out, and reports no class-conditional bias), and the proposal names it and draws that line correctly. What it does do is remove the surrogate-index component from the novelty ledger: fitting success on process features and calibrating it is now published practice, so E7 is a re-application. Also verified and relevant: ProgRM arXiv:2505.18121 and Progress Advantage arXiv:2606.26080 (progress signals for training, not for counterfactual valuation), CUE-R arXiv:2604.05467 (verified; per-evidence-item intervention utility with a role taxonomy, but single-shot RAG and outcome-side endpoints only), Source Attribution in RAG arXiv:2507.04480 (verified; SHAP approximations that minimize costly LLM calls — the cost-reduction-for-attribution slot, though by sampling coalitions rather than by changing the endpoint), the surrogate-outcome methodology paper arXiv:2412.14129 and control variates arXiv:2109.08944 (both verified). COULD NOT VERIFY: DIG arXiv:2509.12765, on which the proposal leans for its G22 framing and for one of its two offline baselines (P4) — 'not found on S2 or HF' on two separate lookups plus a targeted title/mechanism search; treat that citation as unconfirmed. The deeper threat to novelty is not a paper but a textbook fact: replacing a Bernoulli endpoint by a continuous surrogate monotone in it reduces estimator variance, and the proposal cites the very literature (2412.14129, 2109.08944) that establishes this. What is left as new is a single-setting constant (the savings factor on ALFWorld with Qwen3-32B) and a class-bias map whose headline class is manufactured to exhibit the bias it then reports.
reviews.strongest_objection: The central 'class-specific bias' result is definitional, not empirical, and the headline savings prediction has an arithmetic ceiling the proposal never confronts. (1) Bias is defined as deviation from success-LOO, but the whole point of a surrogate is to see what the anchor is too coarse to see. A location-stale item that costs 30 extra steps and still finishes inside the step limit genuinely has negative value to a memory system; calling the step endpoint 'biased' there presupposes that 0/1 success is the only estimand worth having, which the proposal asserts and never argues. P2 then manufactures items designed to lengthen the path without changing success and reports that step endpoints penalize them — the finding is built into the construction, and P7c inherits the same circularity. (2) The proposal validates goal-condition fraction as '1 iff success', so progress = success plus partial credit on the failure subset only. At k=3 the reader succeeds ~0.81/0.87, so all the variance reduction must come out of a ~13-19% failure mass; a 3x cut in retrievals for the same rank reliability is a strong demand on that sliver, and the design never shows the arithmetic. Compounding this, the headline P1 has a dead zone: the prediction is savings >= 3x and the falsifier is savings < 1.5x with the CI excluding 3x, so a measured 2.2x — arguably the single most likely outcome — neither confirms nor falsifies. (3) The entailment check's three 'unresolvable' verdicts are real and unfixed: P5's per-pair interaction at 20 paired episodes carries a CI of roughly +/-30-40 net, so almost no pair can be flagged under either endpoint and the '<= 30% of redundant pairs' falsifier fires regardless of truth; P3a's confirming rule (CI excluding 0.3) and falsifying rule (CI below 0.4) are 0.1 apart against a bootstrap half-width of 0.15-0.2, so [0.32, 0.38] satisfies both; P7c is a ratio whose denominator is never sized in raw steps. (4) A concrete methodological bug: E7 regresses success on a feature set containing goal-condition fraction, which the design validates as exactly 1 iff success. That is perfect separation — an unpenalized logistic fit does not converge, and any fit that does will load onto that feature, driving index-LOO toward success-LOO and making P3b and P3c null by construction rather than by evidence. Three predictions unresolvable, two near-null by construction, and a headline with an indeterminate middle leaves roughly three of eight predictions capable of discriminating.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: Four changes, in order of importance. (1) Argue the estimand instead of assuming it. Either justify why 0/1 success is the ground truth a memory curator wants (and then the 'bias' finding stands), or define value on a stated utility over success and cost (steps, tokens, wall-clock) and report where the endpoints disagree with THAT — at which point step endpoints are not biased but measuring a different, defensible thing, and the paper becomes about which estimand a curator should buy. (2) Fix the headline. Pre-register the exact progress functional; decompose the predicted variance reduction into the success-pinned top and the failure-subset partial credit, and show in the pilot what fraction of episodes carries usable partial credit; then set a single threshold with a stated MDE (e.g. savings >= 2x with the CI excluding 1.3x) so there is no dead zone between prediction and falsifier. Report the stale-class progress value separately on the success and failure subsets. (3) Fix E7. Drop any success-determining feature from the index (or pre-register penalization and report the fitted weights), and report the class biases with the goal-condition feature in and out of the fit; without this P3b/P3c cannot fail. (4) Cut to fund power. P5 as written is uninformative — either pool the interaction across pairs for both endpoints or raise per-pair episodes to where a 10-net interaction is detectable (~200/pair), and state the per-pair MDE; measure the raw-step stale penalty in the pilot and size E4's instance-location cell from it as an absolute step reduction. Dropping P5 and E5 entirely would fund a properly powered P1/P2/P3 and lose little.
reviews.missing_baseline: Covariate-adjusted success-LOO — the CUPED / control-variate baseline that needs no new endpoint and no new instrumentation. Every LOO delta is already paired to an intact-set run on the same (game, seed); regressing the success delta on pre-treatment covariates available for free (the base run's outcome, game task type, the k=0 or static3 difficulty of that game, retrieval rank/score) is the standard variance reduction for exactly this design, and the proposal's own related work cites the control-variate literature (verified arXiv:2109.08944) without instantiating it as an arm. This is the baseline that can sink the paper: if adjusting the success endpoint on the base-run outcome and task type buys 2x for free, the process-endpoint program's headline 3x has almost no incremental value while carrying all the class bias the paper documents. A reviewer will also ask for the trivial compute-matched comparator the plan never states — the same total episode budget spent on more (game, seed) retrievals under plain success-LOO — since 'fewer re-runs at fixed reliability' is only interesting relative to what the extra re-runs would have bought. Secondarily, the second offline surrogate should include a no-forward-pass control (retrieval score / rank of the item, and item-type match), which is free and is what a practitioner would actually reach for before running any of this.
reviews.preprint_collision: No verified collision on the central claim, but the check has one real gap and one over-claim. Queries I ran, all answered by the literature command (Semantic Scholar + HF, both ok; WebSearch unavailable this session, WebFetch not used): (a) 'surrogate endpoint variance reduction binary success outcome per-item counterfactual value estimation' — nothing on per-item counterfactuals; nearest are clinical/statistical (arXiv:2412.14129, arXiv:2602.03730) and RAG-adjacent counterfactual prompting (arXiv:2605.01048). (b) --recent 'process signal partial progress instead of binary success reduces rollouts needed to estimate per-example contribution LLM agent memory' — returned EarlyEval arXiv:2609.02783 (2026-09-02), IAPO arXiv:2608.24588, TRIAGE arXiv:2606.32017, Progress Advantage arXiv:2606.26080, Echo Gap arXiv:2608.00017; all are policy-training credit or aggregate evaluation, none estimates per-item counterfactual value. (c) closest named method, 'DIG document influence generation confidence gain retrieval-augmented attribution scoring documents' — returned nothing matching DIG; see the ID verification below. (d) home vocabulary, 'data valuation leave-one-out proxy metric cheaper evaluation signal variance reduction influence estimation' — DataInf arXiv:2310.00902, DVGS arXiv:2405.08217, arXiv:2607.25356 (proxy-guided sampling for data quality loses to uniform sampling); nothing on surrogate endpoints for LOO. (e) --recent 'surrogate outcome bias subgroup surrogate paradox partial credit metric misranks interventions' — 4 results, none relevant, reported as empty. (f) 'CUPED variance reduction A/B test surrogate index long-term outcome' — no CUPED paper returned, which corroborates the proposal's query (1); this is an indexing gap in the tool, not evidence that CUPED does not exist, and the proposal is right to cite Deng 2013 / Athey 2019 from memory but should say so as unverified. (g) --recent 'which retrieved memory item helped ablation removal re-run experience bank agent per-item utility' — CUE-R arXiv:2604.05467, Compliance Trap arXiv:2607.10608, A-MAC arXiv:2603.04549; nothing on endpoint substitution. (h) 'goal-condition success rate partial credit metric ALFRED ALFWorld subgoal progress' — nothing directly on point. ID verification: I verified arXiv:2609.02783, arXiv:2606.26080, arXiv:2505.18121, arXiv:2412.14129, arXiv:2604.05467, arXiv:2507.04480 and arXiv:2109.08944 by direct lookup. I could NOT verify arXiv:2509.12765 (DIG) — two separate 'paper' lookups returned 'not found on S2 or HF' and a targeted mechanism search surfaced nothing matching it. DIG is named in the proposal's Related Work as the G22 anchor and supplies one of the two offline surrogates in P4, so an unverifiable ID there is a live weakness; the proposal should either fix the ID or drop the dependency. I did not attempt to verify arXiv:2606.00547, arXiv:2602.23440 or arXiv:2607.21106 (they support framing, not the novelty argument). Judgment on the check itself: it is genuinely done — four queries, IDs given, one home-vocabulary query with no agent/memory words, both channels reported — and above this program's usual standard. Two deductions: it never searched the ALFRED/ALFWorld goal-condition-success-rate literature, where partial-credit progress has been a standard reported metric since 2020, so the framing of process endpoints as a new instrument is unsupported; and it under-reads EarlyEval, which as verified trains and calibrates a success classifier over behavioral features one week earlier and therefore makes the E7 surrogate index a re-application rather than a new component.
